  • Health Department staff Joseph Botelho provided an overview regarding the

  • Member Diles III joined the meeting at 12:43 p.m.

  members shared thoughts on how to strengthen the homelessness system
  within the upcoming year. The goal of the activity was to connect the

2.  26-56211  Recommendation to receive and file a presentation from the Ethics Department
  and the City Attorney’s Office on the 2026 Annual Ethics Update, including the
  Brown Act and Robert’s Rules of Order.

  • City staff from the Ethics Office Heather Van Wijik provided a presentation to
  the board regarding Ethics and Transparency. She provided updates
  regarding the 2026 priorities to building a stronger Ethics and Transparency
  Program.
  • Key take aways included guidance on Ethical decision making, fairness and
  process matter, required trainings and information regarding the Ethics
  Helpline. Additional resource information was provided for Board members to
  access.
  • The City of Long Beach Health Department City Attorney Nicholas Masero
  provided a presentation on Brown Act and Roberts’s Rules of Order.
  • The presentation included key take away points:
  o The Brown Act: Ensures that public business is conducted openly,
  transparently, and with opportunities for public participation.
  o Robert’s Rules of Order: Provides procedures for conducting
  meetings, making motions, facilitating discussion, and taking votes.
  o The boards role in making decisions about the allocation of public
  funding and addressing homelessness in Long Beach.
  o Guidance on agenda material and posting, members of the public
  opportunities to attend and speak during these meetings.
  o Avoiding deliberating on board business outside public meetings.
  o consequences of Brown Act violations.
  o responsibilities of the Chair/Co-Chairs.

  • Health Department staff member Joseph Botelho provided an overview of
  board member attendance requirements, including quorum thresholds. The
  Board currently has 16 seated members, with 9 members required to
  establish a quorum. The Board has a maximum membership of 26 members,
  which would require 14 members to establish a quorum. He also reviewed
  the meeting schedule and board member expectations.
  • The goal is to conduct annual attendance reviews to identify and address
  any attendance-related concerns or issues.
  • A member of the public expressed appreciation to the Committee members
  for their work and dedication.

4.  26-56214  Recommendation to receive and file a presentation on the results of the 2026 Long
  Beach Homeless Count.

  A motion was made by , seconded by , to approve recommendation. The
  motion carried by the following vote:

  • Health Department staff member Dalton Dorr provided an overview of the
  2026 Point-in-Time (PIT) Count, which was conducted on January 22, 2026.
  • Staff presented a percentage-based comparison of PIT Count data overtime.
  The overall number of individuals experiencing homelessness in Long Beach
  increased this year. The unsheltered population remained relatively
  consistent, while the sheltered population increased compared to the
  previous year.
  • Board members comment on the data provided and requested additional
  clarification regarding latinx population.
  • Dalton also provided an update on veteran homelessness, noting that it has
  decreased over the past several years. A collaboration between the VA in
  Long Beach and Orange County, which provides additional resources and
  support services, may have contributed to the reduction among this
  population.
  • Additional data was discussed regarding demographics, family disruptions
  and financial/unemployment percentages.Bureau Manager Rates of
  homelessness in an area are largely impacted by housing affordability.
  • Members of the board provide input on additional information that they would
  like to see added to the 2027 PIT questionnaire.
  • Increasing cost of rentals specifically studios over the past years has
  significantly increased. A third of rental household in this country fall behind
  on rent at some point.
  • Staff and members of the committee had additional conversation regarding
  the information presented and the unsheltered community.

  • Health Department staff Joseph Botelho provided and update on the boards
  recruitment and selection process. The recruitment announcement was
  distributed on September 2, 2026 through the CoC website and email
  listserv. The application deadline in November 13, 2026.
  • No applications have been received through the public application form to
  date. One Long Beach Unified School District Board member has expressed
  interest in serving.
  • Representatives interested include:
  o A City staff representative from the Long Beach Workforce Innovation
  Network (LB WIN).
  o A City staff representative from the City Prosecutor’s Office to
  represent Homeless Court.
  o The school district board member representing elected public officials
  • Staff have contacted potential representatives, including LB WIN, the City
  Prosecutor’s Office, the Long Beach Police Department Quality of Life Team,
  and the Long Beach Chamber of Commerce. The Police Department
  declined the invitation, while the workforce development and Homeless
  Court representatives expressed interest.
  • Members of the board suggested expanding outreach through local social
  media platforms, community-based networks, business associations, and
  personal professional contacts. Members were encouraged to share the
  public recruitment announcement with eligible candidates.
  • Members approved placing the three interested individuals on the next Board
  meeting agenda for review and discussion. This was not an approval of their
  appointments; the Board would consider their information and make a
  decision at a future meeting.

  • Health Department staff Joseph Botelho reviewed the Governance Charter
  and the purpose of standing committees, which conduct systems and policy
  work and develop recommendations for the CoC Board.
  • Existing standing committees include the Access Committee, Coordinated
  Entry System (CES) Committee, Stabilization Committee, and Advisory
  Board with Lived Experience.
  • Staff proposed establishing two additional committees: the Budget and
  Finance Committee and the Youth Advisory Board with Lived Experience.
  • The committee would review quarterly budgets, expenditures, and spending
  patterns to support effective fund utilization and reduce the return of unspent
  funds to HUD.
  • Responsibilities would include reviewing potential funding shifts, developing
  funding priorities, and providing recommendations on funding actions and
  proposed amendments.
  • The committee would provide financial oversight and analysis, while the CoC
  Board would retain final decision-making and approval authority.
  • Staff proposed recruiting members with financial expertise and community
  perspectives, including representatives from the Long Beach Community
  Foundation, United Way, and other regional organizations.
  • Recruitment would consider potential conflicts of interest, particularly among
  individuals affiliated with agencies receiving CoC funding.
  • CoC Board members may participate, and committee chairs may appoint
  members from the general membership.
  • Committees would meet quarterly, approximately four times per year, for an
  estimated 90–120 minutes per meeting.
  • Meetings must be held in person due to Brown Act requirements for these
  standing committees.
  • Health Department staff Alvin Teng added additional information regarding
  the Youth Advisory Board.
  • Staff requested approval to establish the Budget and Finance Committee
  and the Youth Advisory Board with Lived Experience.
  • Board members were invited to consider serving as committee chairs, with
  chair selections potentially deferred to a future meeting.
  • Staff would develop application materials, begin recruitment, and return with
  additional information to finalize committee membership and priorities.
  • Staff anticipated launching the committees in the first quarter of 2027,
  subject to recruitment and member interest.
  • Members approved the recommendation to move forward.

7.  26-56218  Recommendation to receive and file an update on the FY 2026 Continuum of Care
  (CoC) Program Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) Competition.

  A motion was made by Member McFadzen, seconded by Member Shuford, to
  approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  15 Amick, Brown-Shock, Lock, Martins, McFadzen, Muñoz,
  Rockenbach, Scott, Shuford, Tan, Wee, Diles III, Boyce,
  Chamberlain, Williams
  No:  0 None
  Recused: 0 None
  Abstain: 0 None
  Absent: 1 Topolewski

  • Health Department staff Joseph Botelho provided a presentation on updates
  regarding the Notice of Funding Opportunity Competition.
  • The CoC application was submitted on September 30, 2026, in alignment
  with the Board’s August 4 approval. The application, attachments, and
  project applications are available on the CoC website.
  • There is still ongoing Litigation, the FY 2026 NOFO remains subject to
  ongoing legal proceedings. Recent court actions have allowed the
  competition to reopen while challenges to specific NOFO provisions
  continue.
  • The plaintiffs requested relief:
  o Allow HUD to move forward with Tier 1 awards, but without applying
  provisions the court
  o determines to be unlawful.
  o Prevent HUD from making Tier 2 awards until CoCs are given an
  opportunity to submit revised
  o Tier 2 applications without the challenged set-aside and any other
  invalidated provisions.
  o Plaintiffs have also requested temporary relief preventing HUD from
  making awards while the
  o court considers the pending motion.
  o Plaintiffs are no longer asking the court to invalidate the entire FY
  2026 NOFO.
  o Plaintiffs are asking the court to invalidate and prevent HUD from
  applying specific provisions they contend are unlawful, including the
  $1.3 billion set-aside for new projects, service participation
  requirements, harm reduction provisions, law enforcement criteria,
  self-sufficiency criteria, risk review criteria, disability priority, bonus
  limits, and Executive Order-related conditions, among others.
  • No additional action is required at this time.

  application modifications are necessary based on any rulings.
  • Staff will share updates with funded project providers and the CoC through

  December 1, 2026.
